chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman al-Kazzaz, from Sabbah al-Hadda', from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him, 'What do you say about a person in ihram who played with his penis and thereby ejaculated?' He said, 'I consider that he is liable for the same penalty as one who had intercourse with his wife while in ihram: a camel, and he performs Hajj next year.'

key_terms.بَدَنَةً: A camel (specifically used as a sacrificial animal penalty)
key_terms.عَبِثَ: Played with or stimulated (specifically referring to the penis in this context)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim who ejaculates through masturbation while in ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the jurist distinguishes between full sexual intercourse and playful stimulation (tabbith) by equating their legal penalty (kaffarah) to that of sacrificing a camel (badanah) and performing Hajj the following year. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that the severity of the breach of ihram restrictions is determined by the emission of semen and the loss of sexual restraint, rather than solely by the act of penetration, thereby extending the stricter penalty to self-stimulation. The requirement of 'Hajj from the following year' (min qabil) underscores the continuity of the pilgrim's obligation to complete the ritual despite the interruption.
